sections.h2: Who sends the property tax bill in Albany, GA?
sections.html:
The Dougherty County Tax Department sends it. That office collects the county, City of Albany, school board and state property taxes in a single bill, and it also handles real estate, vehicle, personal property, mobile home and timber accounts. The Board of Assessors sits inside the Tax Department and sets the values. For questions call 229-431-3208.

Albany is the county seat of Dougherty County and the only incorporated city in it, so there is no second municipal bill to chase. The city lies on the Flint River in southwest Georgia, about 151 miles south of Atlanta. The 2020 census counted 33,290 housing units in Albany, with 14.0 percent vacant, and a homeowner vacancy rate of 2.3 percent.

Two boards matter here and people confuse them. The Board of Assessors decides what a property is worth and hears value appeals. The Board of Commissioners adopts the millage rate after the digest is final.

sections.h2: When are Albany property taxes due?
sections.html:
Georgia's default is December 20, but a county can move the date by resolution to December 1 or November 15, or bill in installments. The state also gives each taxpayer 60 days from the postmark of the bill before interest starts, so the date printed on your own bill controls.

Recent years have not followed the usual calendar. In November 2025 Dougherty County announced that 2025 bills would mail late because of new state legislative changes, and it set a revised due date of February 20, 2026 with no late fees or penalties for payments made by then. That date has passed. For the 2026 bill, read the due date on the notice itself or call the Tax Department.

sections.h2: What did the 2026 revaluation change for Albany homeowners?
sections.html:
Dougherty County completed its first countywide revaluation in more than ten years, and the 2026 assessment notices carried the new values. The county stresses that an assessment notice is not a tax bill. Taxes are figured after the 45 day appeal period closes, the digest is final and the commissioners adopt the millage rate.

Two state laws shaped the notices. Senate Bill 566 changed the notice format to show the appeal deadline, updated homestead information and estimated savings. Senate Bill 581 created the statewide floating homestead exemption, which can limit increases in the taxable value of a qualifying homestead.

Homeowners with a qualifying 2026 homestead exemption also receive Georgia's one time Homeowner Tax Relief Grant, an $18,000 reduction in assessed value, with no separate application. A house that is not a homestead, such as an inherited rental or a vacant property, does not get that credit.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Albany assessment?
sections.html:
Send a written appeal to the Dougherty County Board of Assessors within 45 days of the date the notice was mailed. The grounds can be taxability, value, uniformity or denial of an exemption. Georgia provides a uniform appeal form.

In that first filing you must pick one of three routes: the county Board of Equalization, a hearing officer, or an arbitrator. The Department of Revenue cannot override the local boards on individual values. Keep copies of any comparable sales, repair estimates and photographs you want the board to see.

sections.h2: What exemptions and special assessments exist in Dougherty County?
sections.html:
The state's standard homestead exemption is $2,000 off the assessed value, and the state's formula multiplies assessed value minus that exemption by the millage rate. Assessed value is 40 percent of fair market value. Apply with the county tax office up to April 1 of the first year you want the exemption, and note that failure to apply counts as a waiver. Ask the Tax Department whether local law adds more.

Dougherty County also offers special assessments through the Board of Assessors:

  • Preferential agricultural assessment, which values qualifying farm property at 30 percent of fair market value rather than 40 percent.
  • Conservation use assessment for certain agricultural, timber, environmentally sensitive and transitional residential land, valued at current use.
  • Forest land protection exemption for land used mainly for growing trees and timber.

Conservation applicants must keep the property in qualifying use for ten years, and the owner can hold no more than 2,000 acres statewide in conservation use programs. A seller of an enrolled tract should ask the Board of Assessors how a sale affects the covenant before signing a contract.

sections.h2: What should an Albany seller know about taxes at closing?
sections.html:
Georgia charges the whole year to whoever owned the property on January 1. The Department of Revenue says no refund is allowed to a partial year owner, so the sales contract and closing statement decide how buyer and seller share the bill.

The real estate transfer tax is $1 for the first $1,000 or fractional part of $1,000 and 10 cents for each additional $100 or fractional part of $100 of sale price. The person who signs the deed is liable, though contracts often shift it to the buyer. It must be paid before the Clerk of Superior Court records the deed, and the seller files the PT-61 declaration electronically through the Georgia Superior Court Clerks' Cooperative Authority.

A home near the Flint River deserves a flood question. Albany's own history includes floods in 1841, 1925, 1994 and 1998, and the city has chosen not to redevelop parts of the riverfront floodplain. Ask the city planning office about floodplain status for a specific address.

sections.h2: What else shapes an Albany house sale besides the tax bill?
sections.html:
Health care, education and the Marine Corps Logistics Base Albany are the city's largest employers, with manufacturing, transportation and retail trade behind them. Phoebe Putney Memorial Hospital anchors the regional health system. Albany State University and Albany Technical College are both in the city, and public schools belong to the Dougherty County School System.

Albany is one of the larger Georgia cities with no interstate. U.S. 19 and U.S. 82 cross the city, and the Liberty Expressway bypasses the north and east sides. An EF3 tornado struck the south side of Albany in January 2017, and Hurricane Michael crossed south Georgia in October 2018. A seller with storm repairs should gather the damage history, permits and receipts for the file.

Whatever the condition, the tax paperwork has the same parts: the Tax Department's bill for the parcel, the Board of Assessors' value and exemption record, and the transfer tax certification the Clerk of Superior Court attaches to the deed.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a delinquent Albany property tax bill?
faqs.a: Call the Dougherty County Tax Department at 229-431-3208. It bills and collects county, city, school and state taxes together.

faqs.q: Does Albany send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Dougherty County Tax Department collects the City of Albany taxes along with the county, school board and state taxes.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal an Albany property value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. File in writing with the Board of Assessors.

faqs.q: Does the $18,000 relief grant apply to a rental house in Albany?
faqs.a: Only homesteads with a qualifying 2026 exemption receive it, so a rental or vacant house does not.

faqs.q: Who pays Georgia transfer tax when an Albany house sells?
faqs.a: The seller is liable under state law, though the sales contract often assigns it to the buyer.
